title: Rise of modern nationalism
summary: France's 1789 Declaration of the Rights of Man held that all sovereignty resides essentially in the nation. As a consequence of the French Revolution and its wars, the idea of a nation began to give people a sense of belonging. It replaced older ideas of dynasty and city-state as the primary focus of political allegiance, and shaped the 19th-century unifications of Germany and Italy.

uncertainty.note: Begins with the French Revolution of 1789, which enshrined the nation as sovereign; 1914 marks the culmination of European imperial nationalism leading to World War I.

as_recorded.value: As a consequence of the French Revolution

where.modern_name: Paris, France (stand-in pin for a movement across Europe)

importance.justification: Modern nationalism redefined the basis of political sovereignty from dynasties to nations, driving nineteenth-century unifications, anti-imperial independence, and global state formation.

related.because: The French Revolution dismantled monarchical absolutism and formally vested political sovereignty in the collective nation.
The Italian Risorgimento applied nationalist ideology to consolidate fragmented regional kingdoms into a unified Italian nation-state.
German nationalist sentiment and Prussian statecraft culminated in the unification of German states into a single nation-state.
Intensified nationalist rivalries and ethnic self-determination struggles destabilized European imperial systems, triggering World War I.
